name: Es Baluard Museu
funding: Govern balear, Consell de Mallorca, Palma council and Fundació d'Art Serra form the foundation. Sponsors: Fundació Baleària, Caixa Colonya, El Corte Inglés, Summum Hotel Group, Hotel Saratoga.
watch: Sponsor names come from the collaborators page. No energy, tobacco, arms or gambling name appears. No protest or censorship found.
records_note: It posts annual reports 2007 to 2025 and accounts 2004 to 2025 with audits, a sponsor logo page, and names its Board of Trustees.

name: Eyebeam
funding: Small nonprofit (revenue $1.63M in 2023), funded by Atlantic, Ford, Jerome and Arison Arts foundations, the NEA, NYSCA and NYC DCLA.
watch: Art-and-technology nonprofit registered in Brooklyn as Eyebeam Atelier Inc. Arison Arts Foundation is Arison-family money.
records_note: Eyebeam's support page names its institutional funders, individual donors and seven board members; its Form 990s are public, but it posts no annual reports.

name: Fabrika Centre for Creative Industries
funding: Self-funded: income of the Oktyabr technical-paper mill and rent of studios, under owner-director Asya Filippova; no major outside investors.
watch: Artist-in-residence programme for foreign artists suspended; Filippova says Fabrika has always lived on self-sufficiency with the owner's support.
records_note: This private creative cluster's site posts no annual reports, accounts, funder list or board; it describes tenants, studios and programmes only.

name: FACT
funding: Arts Council England and Liverpool City Council are statutory funders. Paul Hamlyn, Jerwood, John Ellerman, Granada, Bloomberg Philanthropies and other trusts also give.
watch: More than 260 UK artists asked five London theatres to drop Bloomberg Philanthropies in May 2026; FACT was not named.
records_note: No annual reports found; accounts sit on the Charity Commission register, funders show as undated logos, and the team page names the trustees.

name: FESPACO
funding: About 1.3-1.5bn FCFA executed in 2025 (~US$2.3M), nearly 80% from the Burkina state; EU 195M FCFA, plus the UN, OIF, LONAB lottery and telecoms.
watch: Pan-African film festival, held every two years since 1969. The 2025 edition was nearly 80% state-funded under the military transition.
records_note: No reports, accounts or board posted; partners and media partners blocks show undated logos, and the sponsor slot shows the organiser's logo.

name: Festival International des Arts du Bénin (FInAB)
funding: Run by Groupe Empire's events arm with Benin government support through its arts fund (FDAC). MTN partnered the 2026 edition, Canal+ Impact 2025. Other partners unnamed; no budget published.
watch: Festival in Cotonou, Porto-Novo and Ouidah. The fourth edition closed in early March 2026, with days for Nigeria, Togo, Lebanon and Morocco.
records_note: No FInAB website was found; press names organiser Groupe Empire, the culture ministry and different sponsors each year, with no reports, accounts or board.

name: Fiji Museum
funding: A statutory body on a government grant (F$697,525 operating plus F$500,000 capital in 2018/19). Its digitisation has run on a US Ambassadors Fund grant since 2021.
watch: Its US-funded digitisation grant runs out in Sept 2026, and the museum is seeking F$300k to continue to 2028. UNESCO is also a partner.
records_note: No reports, accounts or funders on its site; annual reports for 2015 to 2017 went to Parliament, later ones lapsed; no trustees named.

name: Firstsite
funding: £2.4M income (FY2025); core funders ACE, Colchester and Essex councils; Garfield Weston, Essex Community Fdn, Attwells Solicitors.
watch: Name to know: Bloomberg Philanthropies Digital Accelerator (Jan 2025). Also a 2018 conflict-of-interest case and a 2026 complaint about nudity in the Duncan Grant show.
records_note: No annual reports; accounts are on the Charity Commission register; a thank-you page names funders, undated; only senior staff are listed, no board.

name: Flutgraben
funding: Self-governing artist cooperative dues, Senate Department for Culture Berlin project grants; non-profit association.
watch: Former bus repair depot on the Spree / Flutgraben canal; self-governing non-profit providing affordable studios for 50+ artists since 1997.

name: Flux Factory
funding: NYSCA, NYC Department of Cultural Affairs, The Andy Warhol Foundation, collective dues; 501(c)(3) non-profit.
watch: Artist-led non-profit collective in Long Island City / Governors Island; collaborative residencies and zero-cost living labs.

name: FOKAL
funding: Open Society Foundations paid a final package in 2024 as it closed its national foundations. Kellogg, Ford and Citi-CAF fund it; the diaspora fund Ayiti Demen raised $609,068.
watch: The EU, AFD and USAID have withdrawn. Gang violence closed Martissant Park to the public.
records_note: Posts annual reports 2016 to 2024 that name funders and an external audit; the board is listed at five members. No financial statements are posted.
